content:
Let the 25 people be positions \(1\) through \(25\), front to back.

For \(i \ge 2\), person \(i\) says “the person in front of me is lying.”  
So if person \(i-1\) lies, person \(i\) tells the truth; if person \(i-1\) tells the truth, person \(i\) lies. Thus truth/lie alternates from position 2 onward.

If person 1 told the truth, then everyone behind would be lying, contradicting the required alternation.  
So person 1 lies.

Then the pattern is:
\[
1: \text{lie},\quad 2: \text{truth},\quad 3: \text{lie},\quad 4: \text{truth},\ldots
\]
Thus all odd-numbered positions lie. Among positions \(1\) through \(25\), there are \(13\) odd positions.

\[
\boxed{13}
\]
